subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.explain: Speed is the distance travelled divided by the time taken.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explain: Acceleration is a change in velocity (m/s) per second, giving units of m/s².

questions.q: Which of these is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Velocity is a vector because it has both size and direction, unlike speed.

questions.q: On a distance-time graph, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?
questions.explain: The gradient of a distance-time graph equals the object's speed.

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, what does the gradient (slope) of the line represent?
questions.explain: The gradient of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration.

questions.q: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explain: The area beneath a velocity-time graph equals the distance travelled.

questions.q: Which equation gives the acceleration of an object?
questions.explain: Acceleration is the change in velocity (final minus initial) divided by the time taken.

questions.q: Which of these is a scalar quantity?
questions.explain: Distance has only magnitude and no direction, so it is a scalar.

questions.q: A horizontal (flat) line on a distance-time graph shows that the object is:
questions.explain: A flat line means distance is not changing, so the object is at rest.

questions.q: A curved line with increasing gradient on a distance-time graph shows that the object is:
questions.explain: An increasing gradient means the speed is rising, so the object is accelerating.

questions.q: A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph shows that the object is moving with:
questions.explain: A flat velocity-time line means velocity is unchanging, so there is no acceleration.

questions.q: What is the main difference between speed and velocity?
options: Velocity includes direction, but speed does not
Speed includes direction, but velocity does not
Velocity is always larger than speed
They are measured in different units
questions.explain: Velocity is speed in a stated direction, making it a vector while speed is a scalar.

questions.q: A line with a negative gradient on a velocity-time graph indicates that the object is:
questions.explain: A negative gradient means velocity is decreasing, so the object is decelerating.

questions.q: An object moves around a circular track at a constant speed. Which statement is correct?
options: Its velocity is changing because its direction changes
questions.explain: Even at constant speed, a changing direction means the velocity (a vector) is changing.

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, a straight line sloping upwards from the origin represents:
questions.explain: A steady upward slope means velocity increases uniformly, so acceleration is constant.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m in 5 s at a steady speed. What is its speed?
A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 30 m/s in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
A velocity-time graph shows an object moving at a constant 10 m/s for 8 s. How far does it travel?
questions.explain: Distance is the area under the graph = 10 m/s × 8 s = 80 m.
